title: Incremental partial-replay runner with per-tenant safety quotas and schema-drift guardrails
creator: Priya Das
description: Goal: Build an incremental partial-replay engine and operator tooling for console analytics pipelines that lets operators run targeted reprocessing windows per-tenant with hard safety quotas, schema-drift detection, and auditable dry-run before mutation. This is driven by a set of recent support cases where long-running backfills caused tenant-wide spikes in cost and temporary metric regressions. The runner should support: 1) selecting a subset of tenants or event-types, 2) resume/skip semantics using resume tokens, 3) per-tenant caps (max events, max tokens, max cpu-hours), 4) preflight dry-run that computes estimated work and diffs without committing, and 5) schema-drift detection that halts and snapshots sample events for manual review when output differs beyond tolerance thresholds.
acceptance_criteria: Operator can submit a partial replay job from Console for a chosen tenant and event-type with explicit numeric safety caps
Dry-run option returns an estimated cost, a sample diff of transformed rows, and a schema-drift score without mutating production tables
Replay runner exposes resume tokens so an operator can pause and resume without duplicate application for previously committed windows
System halts automatically when schema-drift threshold is exceeded and creates an immutable snapshot + ticketable record
Per-tenant quota enforcement is enforced at the runner orchestration layer and reflected in the Console job UI and audit logs
End-to-end tests cover idempotency across retries and validate no double-application of events for the same resume token
notes: Motivation: recent backfills (support incident 2026-01-18) showed that global replays had unpredictable cost and caused temporary churn in derived metrics; operators need a safer stepping-stone tool
We intentionally avoid full cluster-wide backfill orchestration in this ticket; focus is incremental/tenant-scoped jobs to reduce blast radius
Design choice: keep heavy transformation logic inside existing analytics workers; runner acts as coordinator that emits idempotent work units with deterministic 'replay-seq' metadata
Key invariant: every work unit must map to a tamper-proof resume token and an idempotency hash so downstream appliers can ignore duplicates
Console UI will present an estimated 'work footprint' (rows, tokens, cpu-hours) and require a typed confirmation when projected cost exceeds threshold
implementation_plan: API: Add POST /internal/replay-jobs that accepts tenant_id, event_types[], start_ts, end_ts, caps {max_events,max_tokens,max_cpu_minutes}, dry_run boolean
Orchestrator: New incremental-replay service (k8s svc) that slices time windows into shards and emits work records to queue with resume_token and sequence_id
Resume tokens: encode {tenant, event_type, shard_start, shard_end, version} and sign with HMAC to prevent accidental tampering
Idempotency: work records carry canonical event-hash; downstream applier will check replay metadata table before applying a change
Dry-run path: worker processes as usual but writes diffs to a read-only dry_run bucket and aggregates a schema-diff score using jsonschema+statistical delta heuristics
Quotas: orchestration layer enforces caps at job-submission and during runtime; when cap triggered, job pauses and marks 'quota-exhausted' state
Console: Add job creation form, progress view, and a one-click snapshot link for schema-drift events
Telemetry: emit metrics: replay.jobs.submitted, replay.jobs.dry_run_estimated_cost, replay.jobs.applied_events, replay.jobs.paused_quota, replay.schema_drift.alerts
K8s/infra: resource requests for the orchestrator service; autoscaling based on queue-latency and active-job-count
Docs: PRD + runbook for operator steps and emergency abort + rollback instructions
testing_plan: Unit tests for resume token encode/decode and HMAC verification
Property tests to ensure deterministic replay-seq generation for a given input window
Integration test: simulate a tenant-level replay with dry_run true and verify diffs + cost estimates match local simulator
Chaos test: inject worker restarts and ensure resume tokens prevent double-application
E2E staging run: replay a 7-day window for synthetic tenant with caps to validate quota enforcement and console UI flow
Post-deploy canary: limit to 3 internal tenants for 48 hours and monitor replay.jobs.* metrics
observability: Dashboard: Console -> Replays: job list, status breakdown (queued/running/paused/failed/done), per-tenant cost burn rate
Tracing: include replay.job_id on all worker traces and instrument kv-cache hits for re-applied events
Audit log: append immutable job records with submitter, caps, dry_run flag, resume tokens to central audit store (ttl 5 years)
Alerts: replay.schema_drift.alerts -> paged to oncall; replay.jobs.paused_quota -> page owner + ops channel
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: Overlapping replays could create conflicting writes — Mitigation: use tenant-scoped lock and sequence-id ordering; disallow overlapping active windows for same tenant/event_type
Risk: Schema-drift false positives slow operations — Mitigation: allow adjustable tolerance with conservative defaults and require manual approval for automated rollbacks
Risk: Cost underestimation for dry-run — Mitigation: conservative estimators and warn operator; require explicit override for >2x projected cost
Risk: Operator error triggering large job — Mitigation: typed confirmation and billing guardrail that refuses jobs for tenants without cost-ACL
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (internal): deploy orchestrator to staging, enable API, and restrict Console control to internal-only tenants
Phase 2 (canary): enable for 3 pilot customers; monitor metrics and iterate on cost estimator
Phase 3: GA for all tenants with opt-in quota defaults; expose advanced caps to SRE/Platform only
Phase 4: add automated backfill templates for common fixes (eg metric normalization) once we validate idempotency across templates
